newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's October GDP contraction led by fishing.
newsitem.headline: Peru's October GDP contraction led by fishing.

text.p: The 0.8 percent year-on-year contraction of the Peruvian economy in October was led by the fishing sector's 52.3 percent fall in year-on-year output, the National Institute of Statistics and Information (INEI) said Thursday.
Other sectors to contract in October were manufacturing by 3.9 percent and construction by 3.7 percent, the INEI said.

In other areas of the economy, the contraction was in part compensated by a 4.7 percent rise in the agriculture sector, followed by 3.7 percent in mining, 3.1 percent in electricity, 1.4 percent in trade and 0.1 percent in the INEI's "others" category, which encompasses the banking, insurance, transport and government sectors.
The INEI said earlier Thursday the Peruvian economy grew 1.7 percent in the first 10 months of the year, compared with 7.6 percent in the same period of 1995.

The October production figure was the first time the Peruvian economy showed a monthly year-on-year contraction since March, when it registered a figure of minus 1.1 percent. The government is predicting the economy will grow 2.5 percent in 1996.
